unmapped: paths in a DAG with n=d links, each path has at most k=m links

settings.name_in_paper: Mixed adversarial and stochastic regime, oblivious attacker
unmapped: only k_a of the k active links are adversarially attacked; the others are stochastic i.i.d.
settings.definition_quote: This regime assumes that the attacker only attacks $k_a$ out of $k$ active links at each time slot... There is always a $k_a/k$ portion of links under adversarial attack while the other $(k-k_a)/k$ portion is stochastically distributed.

settings.name_in_paper: Mixed adversarial and stochastic regime, theta-memory-bounded adaptive attacker
unmapped: only k_a of the k active links are attacked by a theta-memory-bounded adaptive adversary; the others are stochastic i.i.d.
settings.definition_quote: We consider the same attack model as in the adversarial regime. The difference here is that the attacker only attacks a subset of links of size $k_a$ over the total $k$ links.

unmapped: contamination after tau steps: number of contaminated locations of each suboptimal link up to t is t*Delta(e)*zeta, attacking strength zeta in [0,1/2)

settings.definition_quote: for the oblivious attacker, it selects some slot-link pairs $(t,e)$ as ``locations" to attack before the SPR starts... After certain $\tau$ timslots, for all $t> \tau$ the total number of contaminated locations of each suboptimal link up to time $t$ is $t\Delta(e)\zeta$

algorithms.name: AOSPR-EXP3++ with known gaps (xi_t(e)=c ln(t Delta(e)^2)/(t Delta(e)^2))

source.quote: Under the \emph{oblivious} adversary, no matter how the status of the links change (potentially in an adversarial manner), for $\eta_t = \beta_t$ and any $\xi_t(e) \ge 0$, the regret of the AOSPR-EXP3++ algorithm for any $t$ satisfies R(t) \le 4{k}\sqrt {tn\ln n}.

results.notes: Paper's n (links) mapped to d, path length k mapped to m, t to T. Regret defined as E[sum loss] - min_i E[sum loss_i], treated as pseudo-regret. Polynomial-time via Algorithm 3 (Theorem 19).

tuning: mini-batch size (4k sqrt(n ln n))^(-1/3) t^(1/3)

source.quote: Under the \emph{$\theta$-memory-bounded adaptive} adversary, ..., for $\eta_t = \beta_t$ and any $\xi_t(e) \ge 0$, the regret of the AOSPR-EXP3++ algorithm for any $t$ satisfies R(t) \le (\theta +1){(4{k}\sqrt {n\ln n} )^{\frac{2}{3}}}{t^{\frac{2}{3}}} + o({t^{\frac{2}{3}}}).

results.notes: Bound is exact leading term plus o(t^{2/3}); recorded as O. Proof uses Arora et al. mini-batching, so the quantity is presumably policy regret; batch size depends on t.
